stages.description:
RETRY of stage 5 (pipeline) after the full-journey run recorded an unhandled Playwright error. Root-caused before retrying: src/app/(dashboard)/applications/new/page.tsx's handleCreate() navigates via router.push() (a Next.js client-side transition, confirmed by direct code read), which never fires a browser 'load' event -- the original script's page.waitForURL(regex, {timeout: 20000}) used Playwright's default waitUntil:'load' and hung for the full 20s even if the create+navigate genuinely succeeded, then threw before any before/after DB state could be captured. This retry polls page.url() directly instead of using waitForURL, against the SAME already-existing journey org/user (reused, not recreated) and the SAME real 'Create application' -> 'Move application' UI flow -- no other change to the app or the interaction sequence. ORIGINAL ATTEMPT (kept for transparency, not deleted): the first full-journey run recorded this stage as an unhandled Playwright error before any before/after DB state could be captured (error: "page.waitForURL: Timeout 20000ms exceeded.
=========================== logs ===========================
waiting for navigation until "load"
============================================================"). That failure and its screenshot are preserved below under original_attempt_screenshot and original_attempt_raw_error; it was NOT registered as an app defect in WIRING_GAP_REGISTER.md, since this retry -- reusing the exact same journey org/user/opportunity and the exact same real UI interaction sequence, changing only the test harness's navigation-detection method -- proved the underlying app flow (Apply -> Move application) persists correctly.
stages.action: Create application, then Move application: discovered -> eligibility_review (retry)

assertion.detail: applications.stage updated, real pipeline_history audit rows for both the create and the move -- retry succeeded, confirming the original failure was a test-harness waitForURL/router.push() mismatch, not an app defect
